name: TinaCMS
title: Mica vs. TinaCMS
summary: Both keep content as files in Git and have an official Astro package. TinaCMS edits on the page itself and adds a content index, a hosted service and search. Mica edits in forms beside the real page, and Astro reads the files. Tina suits teams that want on-page editing.

chooseMica.text: You want forms with the real Astro page beside them, and no wiring in each template.
You want Astro to read your files through Content Collections, with types.
You want no content index and no database in the editor.
Your content is on a Git host other than GitHub.
You want to run the editor yourself in one container, behind any OpenID Connect provider.

chooseOther.text: Editors should click on the page to edit it, and see it change as they type. TinaCMS does this, also in Astro.
You want a hosted service (TinaCloud) with plans and support.
You want search over your content, through TinaCloud.
You want an editorial workflow with draft pull requests (Business plan and up).
You want MDX components in your content.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub only, with TinaCloud and with the self-hosted provider. Custom providers are possible.
Hosted service available: TinaCloud. Self-hosting possible: a backend function, a database adapter, a Git provider and an auth provider. The local dev server works without the cloud.
Yes. The Data Layer indexes your content in a database; the files stay the source of truth. TinaCloud hosts it. Self-hosted needs MongoDB or Redis/Vercel KV.
Apache-2.0. The Data Layer packages have a separate licence. Free for 2 users. Team $24 a month for each project. Team Plus $41. Business $249. Enterprise on request.
Yes. Official @tinacms/astro; Astro is the default starter. Content comes through a generated GraphQL client, not Content Collections. The setup adds an SSR adapter.
TinaCloud: GitHub or email. SSO on Enterprise. Self-hosted: Auth.js, Clerk, TinaCloud or custom. OIDC is not documented.
Each save is a commit. The Editorial Workflow (Business and up) uses a branch and a draft pull request. No batch publish is documented.
Yes. Site and editor side by side, in real time in React (useTina); a click on an element opens its form. On Astro, each page is wired by hand with TinaIsland, tinaField() and requestWithMetadata().
Not documented. The documentation names limits of the GitHub API.
Not documented. localContentPath points local development to a separate content repository.
Not documented. The reference field links to collections. Large collections can time out.
Documented patterns, by directory or by field. No locale switcher is documented.
TinaCloud has Admin and Editor. More roles on paid plans. Review is the Editorial Workflow with pull requests (Business).
Planned. An MCP server and AI features are listed as Coming Soon on the roadmap.
